brands.name: Women Worth & Wealth

identity.positioning: A small group money and worth experience for women in New Orleans
identity.offer: Six Wealth Wednesdays, January to April, for 12 women, with the Money Isn't Lucky Summit at the midpoint. Real conversations, practical tools, lasting change.
identity.audience: Smart, capable women who have been made to feel otherwise about money. Earning, raising families, leading teams and building businesses, and quietly carrying the story that they are "just not numbers people." Ready to pour into themselves for once.
identity.wedge: Your worth is the whole picture, not your paycheck. You already own your wealth. The work is learning to steward it.
identity.reviewedBy: Becky's compliance review, before anything is published
identity.tagline: Own your worth. Steward your wealth.
identity.address: New Orleans, LA. Location shared upon enrollment.
identity.title: Created and co-hosted by Amy Landry & Becky Gustafson
identity.credentialsNote: The program is educational. Do not lead with Becky's designations in program marketing, and never use Eternal Wealth Partners, Northwestern Mutual or any broker-dealer name in program copy unless Becky supplies approved disclosure language. Her bio may state her designations and that she founded Eternal Wealth Partners as biographical fact only.
identity.educationalNote: Women Worth & Wealth is an educational program. Content is general in nature and is not financial, tax, or legal advice. Enrollment does not create an advisory relationship with either host. Please consult your own financial, tax, and legal professionals for advice specific to your situation.

voice.heading: How Women Worth & Wealth sounds
voice.source: From the build spec, the site copy and CLAUDE.md in the womens-wealth- repository. If a new piece does not sound like the home page, the piece is wrong.

principles.name: Warm, analytical, visionary
principles.detail: Warm enough that she feels seen, analytical enough that she trusts it, visionary enough that she wants the next chapter. Witty where it helps, never flippant.

principles.name: Speak to a smart woman
principles.detail: Write to one woman who has been made to feel otherwise about money. Never condescend. Never shame. No "even you can" energy.

principles.name: Worth is the whole picture
principles.detail: Her income is one line of her worth. The family she raises, the friends she shows up for and the community she improves are part of it too. Never tie worth to a paycheck.

principles.name: She already owns it
principles.detail: Lead from ownership, not lack. The work is stewardship: understand it, use it on purpose, grow it, protect it.

principles.name: Teach the concept, never the product
principles.detail: How a Roth works, what an emergency fund is for, how compounding behaves. Never "you should buy" anything. No returns, no outcomes, no promises.

principles.name: Real conversations, practical tools, lasting change
principles.detail: Keep the triad. Every piece should leave her with one thing she can try this week.

principles.name: Trace it to a verb
principles.detail: Every piece connects to earn it, use it, grow it or protect it. If it does not, it does not belong.

mechanics: No em dashes and no en dashes anywhere. Use a period, a comma, a colon or parentheses.
Contractions are welcome. This is a warm room, not a letter from a firm.
One question per post is plenty. Two in a row reads as a quiz.
At most one emoji on Instagram, never in the first line. None on LinkedIn.
Name the program in full the first time: Women Worth & Wealth. After that, Worth & Wealth.
Say "Wealth Wednesdays" and "the Money Isn't Lucky Summit" exactly that way.
Educational framing on anything that teaches: a short line that it is general education, not advice.
Amy's lane is worth, leadership and mindset. Becky's lane is the money. Attribute accordingly.
Never fabricate a testimonial, an outcome or a quote. Testimonials wait for the first cohort.

banned.word: earn your worth, know your worth (as a salary line), charge what you're worth

banned.word: financial freedom, get rich, build wealth fast

banned.word: you should invest in, buy, open (any product)
banned.instead: Here is how it works, and what to ask your own professional.

banned.word: guaranteed, results, by month 12 you will have
banned.instead: You will leave with a plan you built yourself.
Nobody taught most of us this. Numbers are learnable.

banned.word: Eternal Wealth Partners, Northwestern Mutual, any broker-dealer
banned.instead: Leave it out of program copy unless Becky supplies approved disclosure language.

banned.word: last chance, only 2 seats left (unless literally true and approved)
banned.instead: Twelve seats, and applications are open.

brands.premise: Marketing Women Worth & Wealth is not a volume problem. Twelve seats fill from one woman reading one post and thinking, that is me. So every piece is written to one woman, names something specific, and invites her into the room rather than selling her a seat.
brands.blurb: Everything Women Worth & Wealth says in public, and what Amy and Becky say to applicants, participants, sponsors and partners between sessions, written once and kept in one place. The thesis comes from the build spec, the substance from the curriculum. Nothing here is approved. Everything here is ready for review.

posts.name: Carousel: "I'm just not a numbers person"
posts.body:
SLIDE 1
"I'm just not a numbers person."

SLIDE 2
That's a story. Not a fact.

SLIDE 3
Somebody handed it to you. A teacher, a parent, a first job, a partner who "handled the money."

SLIDE 4
You run a household. A team. A calendar that would break most people.

SLIDE 5
That is numbers. You've just never been told it counts.

SLIDE 6
Numbers are learnable. Confidence follows competence.

SLIDE 7
Women Worth & Wealth. Six Wealth Wednesdays for 12 women in New Orleans.

CAPTION
"I'm just not a numbers person" might be the most expensive sentence women say.

It isn't true, and it was never yours. It was handed to you, usually before you were old enough to argue.

Session 1 starts here: where your money story came from, and how to rewrite it.

Applications for the first cohort are open. Link in bio.

General education, not financial advice.
posts.note: The wedge post. It names the story nearly every applicant has told about herself. Run it again every month with a new first slide.

posts.name: Your paycheck is one line
posts.body:
Your paycheck is one line of your worth. It was never the whole page.

We keep hearing the same advice aimed at women: earn your worth, charge what you're worth, know your worth before the negotiation.

It sounds empowering. It quietly says your worth is your W-2.

Here's what it leaves out. The family you're raising. The marriage or partnership you're building. The friends you show up for at 11 p.m. The community you make better without anyone asking.

Those aren't side notes to your worth. They are your worth.

Income matters. We'll spend a whole session on asking for more. But we'll do it without tying who you are to the answer.

Women Worth & Wealth starts with a Whole Worth Inventory: every role you hold and the value each one creates. Most women have never written it down.

Own your worth. Steward your wealth.
posts.note: Amy's lane. Post from Amy's profile first; Becky reshares with one line about why she built the program.

posts.name: Carousel: the five numbers
posts.body:
SLIDE 1
Five numbers. That's where it starts.

SLIDE 2
NET WORTH
What you own, minus what you owe.

SLIDE 3
MONTHLY BURN
What it actually costs to run your life for a month.

SLIDE 4
SAVINGS RATE
How much of what comes in, stays.

SLIDE 5
DEBT COST
What your debt charges you, in interest, every month.

SLIDE 6
MONTHS OF RUNWAY
If the income stopped, how long you could keep going.

SLIDE 7
Know these five cold and every money conversation gets easier.

CAPTION
You don't need a finance degree. You need five numbers and an afternoon.

In Session 2 every woman builds a One-Page Financial Snapshot with exactly these five on it.

Save this, then try just one this week. Monthly burn is a good place to start.

General education, not financial advice.
posts.note: The highest save potential in the library. It teaches something she can do tonight.

posts.name: What is the money for?
posts.body:
IMAGE
Cream ground. In Cormorant: What is the money for?

CAPTION
Before the budget. Before the spreadsheet. Before anyone says "should."

What is the money for?

Security. Freedom. Time with your kids. A business of your own. Taking care of your mother. Travel. Rest.

When you know the answer, spending stops being guilt and starts being a choice. That's Values Before Numbers, and it's how Session 2 opens.

Write your three answers in the comments, or just on a sticky note.
posts.note: Invites a comment, which carries the post. Reply to every answer warmly and never with advice.

posts.name: Asking for more without tying your identity to the answer
posts.body:
The hardest part of asking for more isn't the script. It's what the answer seems to say about you.

If they say no, it can feel like a verdict on your worth.

It isn't. It's a price negotiation. Prices get negotiated every day by people who feel nothing about it at all.

What helps:
Research the market rate before the conversation, not during it.
Write the ask down in one sentence and say it out loud twice before you walk in.
Decide in advance what you'll do with a yes, a no, and a "not yet."

And separate the two questions. What is this work worth in the market. And what are you worth as a person. The first one has a number. The second never did.

Session 3 of Women Worth & Wealth pairs Spending on Purpose with Asking for More, and every woman leaves with her own Ask Script.
posts.note: Becky and Amy co-lead Session 3. This one works from either profile.

posts.name: Carousel: tool or trap
posts.body:
SLIDE 1
Debt is a tool. Until it isn't.

SLIDE 2
A tool: it buys something that lasts longer than the payments, at a cost you know.

SLIDE 3
A trap: it buys something that's gone before the payments are.

SLIDE 4
The question isn't "is debt bad." It's "what is this debt costing me, every month, in interest."

SLIDE 5
Write every debt down. Balance, rate, minimum. That's a Debt Map.

SLIDE 6
Most women feel better the minute it's on one page. Even before anything changes.

CAPTION
Shame keeps debt in a drawer. A page brings it out where you can do something about it.

In Session 4 we build a Debt Map together, then talk through how a payoff order actually works.

General education, not financial advice.
posts.note: Concept only. Never recommend a product, a lender or a specific payoff method as the right one for her.

posts.name: What the stock market is, really
posts.body:
If you've ever nodded along when someone mentioned "the market" and quietly hoped nobody asked you a follow up, you're in very good company.

Here's the one sentence version: owning a share means owning a small piece of a real company, and its value moves with what people believe that company will be worth.

Everything else (funds, indexes, time horizons) builds from that.

We teach the vocabulary in Session 4, so the next time it comes up you can ask a better question.

General education, not financial advice.
posts.note: Becky's lane. Educational framing at the foot, every time.

posts.name: Carousel: if something happened tomorrow
posts.body:
SLIDE 1
If something happened to you tomorrow, who would it land on?

SLIDE 2
Who knows where everything is?

SLIDE 3
Are your beneficiaries still the people you'd choose today?

SLIDE 4
Is there a reserve, so a hard month doesn't become a hard year?

SLIDE 5
Has anyone you love heard what you'd want?

SLIDE 6
Protecting what you've built is an act of love, not a gloomy chore.

CAPTION
The women everyone depends on are often the ones with nothing written down.

Session 5 is Protecting What You've Built, with a Protection Checklist and a beneficiary audit you can finish in an evening.

One task for this week: look up who is listed as beneficiary on one account. Just one.

General education, not financial advice.
posts.note: Tender subject. Warm, never alarming, no scare statistics.

posts.name: The money conversation nobody had with us
posts.body:
Most of us learned about money by watching. Very few of us were ever sat down and told.

So the conversation keeps not happening. With a partner. With aging parents. With kids who are watching us now, the way we watched.

It doesn't have to be a big, formal talk. It can start with one question at dinner: what's one thing your family taught you about money, without ever saying it?

In Session 5 we practise these conversations out loud, in a room where nobody is going to judge the answer, with a Family Money Conversation Guide to take home.

Real conversations. Practical tools. Lasting change.
posts.note: Becky leads, with Amy. Works well on Facebook too.

posts.name: Twelve women, one table
posts.body:
IMAGE
A real photograph of a breakfast table set for twelve. No faces needed.

CAPTION
Twelve women. One table. Breakfast at every session.

No stupid questions and no sales pitch.

That's the whole design of Women Worth & Wealth. Six Wealth Wednesday mornings, January to April, in New Orleans, with the same 12 women every time.

Amy brings the worth. Becky brings the wealth.

Applications are open. Link in bio.
posts.note: Use a real photo of the room once it exists. Until then, a styled table, never a stock photo of women at laptops.

posts.name: Money isn't lucky
posts.body:
Shonda Rhimes said it better than we could: don't call her lucky.

Lucky implies nothing was done. That something was handed over.

The women who seem lucky with money are usually intentional with it. They made a hundred small choices, mostly where nobody could see.

That's the idea behind the Money Isn't Lucky Summit, on Wednesday, March 17, at the midpoint of the first Women Worth & Wealth cohort. A morning on how beliefs become choices and choices become a life.

It seats 24: the 12 women of the cohort and 12 women from outside it.

Details at wealthandwisdom.biz.
posts.note: Quote is attributed in the source (Year of Yes). Keep the attribution whenever the quote is used.

posts.name: Pay it forward
posts.body:
Some of the women who would gain the most from this room can't pay for a seat in it.

That's what a Pay-It-Forward seat is for. A sponsor funds a full seat in the Women Worth & Wealth cohort, and the seat is awarded by application to a woman who could not otherwise attend. It includes her ticket to the Money Isn't Lucky Summit.

If your company, your firm or your family has been looking for a way to put real money behind women's financial confidence in New Orleans, this is a very direct one.

There are smaller ways to help too, down to hosting a single breakfast.

Message Amy or me, or see the options at wealthandwisdom.biz/sponsor.

engagement.body:
Subject: Meet your accountability partner

{{first}}, meet {{NAME}}. {{NAME}}, meet {{first}}.

You'll check in with each other briefly between sessions. Fifteen minutes is plenty. Ask each other one question: did you do the one thing?

That's it. Be kind, be honest, cheer loudly.

Amy & Becky

engagement.name: Inviting a friend to the Summit
engagement.body:
Subject: Money Isn't Lucky

Hi {{first}},

On Wednesday, March 17, we're hosting the Money Isn't Lucky Summit: a morning on why the women who seem lucky with money are usually intentional with it.

It seats 24. Twelve seats are for our cohort and twelve are for women like you.

Details and tickets are at wealthandwisdom.biz. We'd love to have you in the room.

Becky
engagement.note: Only to people who opted in or whom you know personally.

engagement.name: Thanking a sponsor
engagement.when: Within a day of a sponsorship commitment
engagement.body:
Subject: Thank you

{{first}},

Thank you. Because of you, {{ONE_SPECIFIC}}.

We'll keep you posted on how the cohort goes, and we'd love to see you at the Summit on March 17.

Before we thank you publicly, could you confirm how you'd like to be named?

With real gratitude,
Amy & Becky
engagement.note: Never name a sponsor publicly before they confirm the wording.

engagement.name: The note after the last session
engagement.body:
Subject: Your next chapter

Hi {{first}},

Four months ago you walked in with a money story. You walked out with a plan you built yourself.

You're part of the alumnae network now. We'll be in touch with gatherings, and the door is always open.

One request: if this room mattered to you, tell one woman about it.

With love,
Amy & Becky
engagement.note: Ask for testimonials separately, in writing, with permission to use. Never draft one for her.

engagement.name: Replying to a comment
engagement.when: Within two hours of the comment
engagement.body: Thank you, {{NAME}}. So many women tell us the same thing. {{ONE_SPECIFIC}}
engagement.note: Two sentences at most. Never answer her specific financial situation in public.

engagement.name: Replying to a DM about the program
engagement.body:
Hi {{NAME}}! Thank you for reaching out.

Short answer: {{GENERAL_PRINCIPLE}}.

Everything about the program (dates, what's included, how to apply) is at wealthandwisdom.biz. And if you'd like to talk it through, Amy or Becky would be glad to.
engagement.note: Warm and quick. Point to the site rather than pasting pricing into DMs.

sequences.name: A business or firm that might sponsor
sequences.who: A company, firm or family foundation that cares about women in New Orleans
sequences.when: You have a name and no warm path yet

steps.name: The connection note
steps.body: {{first}}, I love what {{client.entity}} does for women in New Orleans. Would be glad to be connected.
steps.ifNoReply: If not accepted in 14 days, stop and look for a warm introduction instead.

steps.name: After they accept
steps.body:
Thanks for connecting, {{first}}.

Amy Landry and I are starting Women Worth & Wealth in January: six Wealth Wednesdays for 12 women, on owning their worth and stewarding their wealth. Educational, in person, in New Orleans.

No ask today. If it ever lines up with what {{client.entity}} cares about, I'd love to tell you more over coffee.
steps.ifNoReply: No third message on this branch for a month. Engage with their posts instead.

steps.name: The specific invitation
steps.body:
Subject: A seat for a woman who could not otherwise come

{{first}},

One very direct way to help: a Pay-It-Forward seat funds a full place in the cohort for a woman who could not otherwise attend, awarded by application. There are smaller options too, down to hosting a single breakfast.

Everything is at wealthandwisdom.biz/sponsor. Would twenty minutes be worth it?

Becky
steps.ifNoReply: Stop here. Invite them to the Vision Board party instead.

sequences.note: Three touches over a month, two of which ask for nothing.

sequences.name: A sponsor you already know
sequences.who: Someone in your network who has supported women's causes before
sequences.when: Any time, ideally before the launch party

steps.name: The personal ask
steps.body:
Subject: Something Amy and I are building

{{first}},

You're one of the first people I thought of. Amy Landry and I are starting Women Worth & Wealth in January, and some of the women who would gain the most from it can't pay for a seat.

Would you consider a Pay-It-Forward seat, or a smaller piece like a breakfast? I'd love to tell you about it over coffee.

Becky
steps.ifNoReply: Follow up once, by phone, after a week.

steps.name: Call them
steps.body: No email. Pick up the phone. Ask how they are first.

sequences.note: Warm asks go personal and short.

sequences.name: A women's organisation that could partner
sequences.who: NAWBO, ABWA, Power of Women, a university women's leadership program, a professional women's network

steps.name: The partnership note
steps.body:
Subject: Women Worth & Wealth and {{client.entity}}

{{first}},

Amy Landry and I are launching Women Worth & Wealth in January: a small group, educational experience for 12 women on money and worth.

We'd love to offer {{client.entity}}'s members an invitation to the Vision Board launch party on January 7, and to talk about whether a partnership makes sense.

Could we find twenty minutes?

Amy & Becky
steps.ifNoReply: Follow up once after ten days.

steps.name: One follow up
steps.body: {{first}}, floating this back up in case it got buried. Happy to work around your calendar.
steps.ifNoReply: Stop. Revisit before the next cohort.

sequences.note: Amy and Becky both have long histories in these organisations. Use the warm path wherever one exists.

sequences.name: A woman engaged with something you published
sequences.who: Commented, replied, or sent a DM about the program

steps.name: The reply that does not pitch
steps.ifNoReply: No follow up. She engaged once, which is not permission. Keep publishing.

steps.name: Watch, do not chase
steps.body: No message. Engage warmly with her posts for a few weeks. A second engagement is a different signal.

sequences.note: The restraint is the point. Chasing is what teaches women not to engage.

sequences.name: After the interest form
sequences.who: A woman who filled in the intake on the site but has not applied

steps.name: A personal note
steps.body:
Subject: Thank you for raising your hand

Hi {{first}},

Thank you for telling us a little about yourself. We read every one.

If you have questions before applying, just reply. And if the timing isn't right this year, that's fine. We'll keep you posted on the next cohort.

Amy & Becky
steps.ifNoReply: One more note in two weeks, then the monthly list only.

steps.name: The gentle reminder
steps.body: Hi {{first}}, a quick note that applications for the first cohort are still open at wealthandwisdom.biz/apply. No pressure at all.

sequences.name: After the Vision Board party
sequences.who: Anyone who came to the launch party

steps.name: Thank you for coming
steps.body:
Subject: Your vision board

Hi {{first}},

Thank you for coming last night. We hope your vision board is somewhere you'll see it every day.

If you're thinking about the cohort, applications are open at wealthandwisdom.biz/apply. And if a friend would love it, send her our way.

Amy & Becky
steps.ifNoReply: No follow up beyond the monthly note.

sequences.note: Send within a day while the evening is fresh.

sequences.name: Not this cohort
sequences.who: A woman who would love it but the timing is wrong

steps.name: Honour the no
steps.body:
Hi {{first}},

Completely understood, and thank you for telling us. We'll keep you on the list for the next cohort, and the monthly note will keep coming if you'd like it.

Amy & Becky
steps.ifNoReply: Next contact: when the next cohort opens.

options:
Women Worth & Wealth is a small group, in person experience for women in New Orleans who want to stop being afraid of their money and start acting as its stewards. Six Wealth Wednesdays, January to April, for 12 women, with the Money Isn't Lucky Summit at the midpoint. Created and co-hosted by Amy Landry and Becky Gustafson.

Women Worth & Wealth is an educational program and does not provide financial, tax, or legal advice.

calendar.heading: The launch quarter, week by week
calendar.note: Twelve themed weeks that build toward the Vision Board party on January 7 and the first Wealth Wednesday on January 27. The studio counts week 1 from the start of the current quarter, so slide the weeks if the launch lands elsewhere. Each week names the carousel, the Reel and the brief for the live post.
rhythm: Tuesday is the carousel. Wednesday is the Reel. Thursday is written that week from something real.
Monday prepares and submits to Becky's review. Friday replies and reads the numbers. Neither posts.
LinkedIn takes two a week between the two hosts.
One email a month to the interest list, on the first Tuesday.
The week of Christmas is lighter on purpose. Use it to record January.
liveSlotSources: A question a woman asked you this week, without anything identifying, answered in general.
A money belief you were handed and when you noticed it.
Something you saw at a women's event, with a photo of people (with permission).
A preparation moment: the workbook arriving, the breakfast menu, the room.
A thing you changed your mind about.
A sponsor or partner thank you, once they have approved the wording.
